Home / Our practice

Clear thinking. Workable change.

Senior business analysis and governance advisory for organisations where people, processes and systems need to work together.

Discuss your needs →

Connect the evidence. Make the next decision clear.

Axiomotl is a senior-led advisory practice for the gap between an organisational ambition and a change people can use. We examine the current situation, define what must change and identify who will own the decisions and operations that follow.

That work brings together business analysis, process governance, requirements, procurement support and transition into business-as-usual. An engagement may begin with a specific question, a difficult handover, or a programme that needs a clearer basis for its next decision.

The receiving team leaves with usable evidence, named responsibilities and documentation it can maintain.

Dr Ramzi Abbassi

BMedSc (Hons)PhDCertification of Capability in Business Analysis (CCBA)

Scientific understanding.
Operational perspective.

Ramzi brings a background spanning scientific research, research operations, laboratory digitalisation and enterprise business analysis. His August 2026 author biography describes a focus on scientific digital transformation, with work across governance, operating models, data migration, rollout strategy and transition to everyday operations. Read his implementation perspective.

In a February 2024 interview, he described laboratory experience at the University of Sydney, UNSW and the University of Oxford, and research support work at the Children’s Cancer Institute Australia involving safety and compliance. The interview also records his move from using eLabNext within a research organisation to joining its team as a Lab Digitalisation Specialist, supporting users across Australia, New Zealand and the wider Asia Pacific. Read the interview.

This background helps translate requirements between specialist users, business owners, technology teams and vendors.

The organisations named here describe Ramzi’s published professional background, not Axiomotl client endorsements.

Where that experience matters

Complexity often sits between teams, rather than within a single system.

Research and regulated environments

Scientific platforms bring together sample records, protocols, data access and reporting. We help make requirements, ownership and decision pathways explicit so that different groups can work to an agreed set of expectations.

Technology and vendor decisions

A product demonstration is only part of the evidence. We connect user needs, evaluation criteria, process dependencies and implementation constraints so a team can compare options and explain its decisions.

Transition into operations

Go-live is a milestone, not the end of the work. We help define readiness, support responsibilities, training and escalation paths so the receiving team knows what it owns and how to keep the service working.

How we work with you

Start with the actual work

Understand how people make decisions and move information today. Test assumptions against evidence, stakeholder conversations and the constraints of the organisation.

Make ownership visible

Agree who decides, who contributes and where exceptions go. Keep requirements, controls and decisions connected so the reasoning stays understandable.

Build for the receiving team

Make outputs useful beyond the engagement. Process maps, decision records, readiness checks and handover materials should support the people responsible for the next step.

Explore our approach →

Choose the support the work needs.

A focused diagnostic can establish what is happening and which decisions matter next. Requirements and decision architecture provide a basis for delivery or procurement. Transition and operating-model work prepares the organisation for everyday ownership. Embedded advisory adds senior analysis alongside an existing team.

Scope begins with the situation, the decision ahead and the outcomes your team needs to own.

Explore our services →

pages.description: A clear path through complex work. Understand the situation, work through the options and prepare people to act.
pages.html:
Skip to content
HomeOur PracticeOur ApproachOur ServicesContact
Discuss your needs
HomeOur PracticeOur ApproachOur ServicesContact
Home/Our approach

A clear path through complex work.

Understand the situation, work through the options and prepare people to act. The starting point and depth of work depend on the problem you need to solve.

Discuss your needs →

Working together

Agree the focus before the work begins.

You bring the context. Together, we agree the questions, the people to involve and the outputs the work needs to produce.

Proportionate to the problem

These stages guide the work; they do not prescribe a fixed programme. An engagement may focus on a diagnostic, a specific decision or preparation for handover.

Evidence people can use

Review findings with the people affected. Keep assumptions visible, record the reasoning behind decisions and leave material the team can work with.

01 / Analyse

Build a shared account of the problem.

What is happening, and what evidence supports that view?

Start with the work as it happens today. Bring together the people involved, the available evidence and the decisions that are proving difficult.

What we work through

Walk through the current process, including exceptions and workarounds. Identify where information changes hands, where controls are missing and who is affected. Test assumptions with the people doing the work.

What you take forward

An agreed problem statement, a current-state view and a prioritised set of questions to resolve.

02 / Design

Shape options that fit the operating context.

What would need to change for each option to work?

Translate the findings into practical requirements and possible ways forward. Consider how each option would affect people, processes, systems and governance.

What we work through

Map the proposed workflow and interfaces. Clarify the requirements and their rationale, then examine constraints, dependencies and trade-offs with stakeholders. Where procurement is involved, make evaluation criteria explicit.

What you take forward

Traceable requirements, workable options and criteria the team can use to compare them.

03 / Implement

Turn the selected direction into delivery.

What must happen, who owns it and what will Transition need?

Convert the agreed direction into sequenced delivery work. Keep owners, dependencies, risks and operational preparation visible.

What we work through

Confirm scope and acceptance criteria, sequence the work and assign owners. Track dependencies and unresolved risks, and involve the receiving team before handover planning begins.

What you take forward

A delivery plan with accountable owners, agreed controls and the inputs needed to prepare Transition.

04 / Transition

Prepare the receiving team for everyday operations.

Can the receiving team run and support the work?

A project handover needs more than a completion date. Establish what the receiving team will own and what must be ready before the work moves into business as usual.

What we work through

Check operational readiness with the teams involved. Define roles, support arrangements and escalation routes. Agree the training, documentation and assurance needed for a usable handover.

What you take forward

A transition plan, clear responsibilities and agreed readiness criteria, supported by handover material.

05 / Sustain

Review what happens after the change.

Is the change working, and what needs attention next?

Use evidence from everyday work to see whether the change is doing what was intended. Keep ownership and review arrangements clear as circumstances develop.

What we work through

Agree what to monitor and when to review it. Examine recurring exceptions and feedback with the responsible team, then decide whether processes, controls or support arrangements need adjustment.

What you take forward

Review points, named owners and a record of actions to address emerging issues.

Start with the decision ahead

Where does your team need support?

Explore the services or tell us about the situation. We can agree a useful starting point and the scope of work from there.

HomeOur PracticeOur ApproachOur ServicesContact

HomeOur PracticeOur ApproachOur ServicesContact
Home/Our services

Business analysis & governance

The right support for the work ahead.

Choose a focused review or senior analysis alongside your team. Start with the problem, the people affected and the decision ahead.

Discuss your needs →

Four ways to work with us.

Choose the level of support that fits the situation: diagnose the current state, structure a decision, prepare operational ownership or add senior analysis to the team.

Decision architecture connects requirements, evidence, options, owners and decisions. An operating model sets out everyday ownership, responsibilities and support. A governance healthcheck reviews whether decisions, controls and accountabilities are working. A principal business analyst is a senior practitioner who works across complex stakeholders and delivery questions.

Business & Governance Diagnostic

→

Understand where work stalls, responsibilities blur or the same issue keeps returning. Build a shared picture before deciding what to change.

Requirements & Decision Architecture

→

Turn complex needs into clear, prioritised decisions, with pragmatic options and a route to implementation.

BAU Transition & Operating Model

→

Turn plans into everyday practice, with clear processes, roles and measures that stick.

Embedded Principal BA Advisory

→

Work alongside your team as a trusted advisor, bringing senior analysis, structure and momentum when it’s needed most.

Understand the current state

Business & Governance Diagnostic

Discuss your needs →

Find where work stalls, why the same issues return and which causes to address first.

When it helps

Handoffs keep breaking down. Teams rely on workarounds, or it is unclear who owns a decision. You need a shared account of what is happening before choosing a fix.

What the work involves

Map the current process with the people involved. Examine exceptions and control gaps, trace recurring problems to their causes, and agree which decisions need attention.

Outputs to agree in the scope

  • Current-state and stakeholder analysis
  • Root causes and control gaps
  • Prioritised decisions and actions

The diagnostic gives your team an evidence base for deciding what to tackle next.

Make the decision explicit

Requirements & Decision Architecture

Discuss your needs →

Turn operational and regulatory needs into requirements that can be traced to the decisions they support.

When it helps

Stakeholders describe the problem differently. Requirements are difficult to compare, or a procurement decision needs clearer evaluation criteria.

What the work involves

Clarify the needs with stakeholders and map how processes connect. Establish the evidence for each requirement, compare the options and make decision ownership explicit.

Outputs to agree in the scope

  • Requirements and traceability
  • Process, interface and decision maps
  • Procurement and evaluation artefacts

Keep the reasoning alongside the requirement, so the team can explain why it matters.

From project to practice

BAU Transition & Operating Model

Discuss your needs →

Work out what must be ready before go-live, and how the receiving team will run and support the work afterwards.

When it helps

A project is nearing handover, but everyday responsibilities are still unclear. The receiving team needs a workable support model and material it can use.

What the work involves

Assess readiness for business as usual (BAU). Define roles and governance, work through support arrangements, and identify the training and handover material the team needs.

Outputs to agree in the scope

  • Readiness and transition assessment
  • Governance, roles and support model
  • Handover, training and assurance

Make the conditions for a usable handover clear before the project closes.

Senior support alongside your team

Embedded Principal BA Advisory

Discuss your needs →

Bring an experienced business analyst into work that needs sustained attention across stakeholders and decisions.

When it helps

Your team needs senior analysis as the work develops, rather than a single standalone assessment. Stakeholder needs or vendor choices require ongoing scrutiny.

What the work involves

Work alongside your team on the agreed priorities. Support executive decisions, examine stakeholder and vendor questions, and review governance as circumstances change.

Outputs to agree in the scope

  • Executive decision support
  • Complex stakeholder and vendor analysis
  • Governance healthchecks and course correction

Agree the focus and responsibilities around the support your team actually needs.

Start with the situation

Not sure which service fits?

Tell us where the work is stuck and the decision ahead. We can discuss a defined piece of work or support alongside your team, then agree the scope and outputs.
